name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Houses a 28-foot gilded Buddha statue, ancient manuscripts, and is the spiritual heart of the Monpa community. Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama; overlooks the Tawang Chu valley.
facts: Founded 1680-81 following wishes of 5th Dalai Lama
Famous for Torgya and Losar festivals

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake formed by an earthquake, famous for upright dead tree trunks rising from the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood film shoot. Located on the route toward Bum La Pass amid alpine scenery.
facts: Formed by earthquake creating submerged forest

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at about 4,170 m on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang with stunning Himalayan views, often snow-covered; nearby Sela Lake freezes in winter. Now complemented by Sela Tunnel for all-weather access.
facts: Named after local Monpa woman Sela

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular ~100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town, cascading into the Nuranang Chu. Easily accessible from the main highway between Sela Pass and Tawang; small hydel plant at base. Featured in Bollywood films.
facts: About 40 km from Tawang near Jang
Best during monsoon for full flow
Originates from slopes of Sela Pass

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Buddhist monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Founded around 1489; smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, with spiritual significance for the region.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial in the form of a Buddhist stupa dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features names of fallen soldiers, light and sound shows, and overlooks the town amid prayer flags.

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4,600 m on the India-China Line of Actual Control. Historic trade and 1962 war route; Border Personnel Meeting Point. Restricted access requiring special permits from army/administration.
facts: Site of 1962 Battle of Bum La

name: Pangateng Tso (PT Tso)
description: Scenic high-altitude lake near Tawang, popular for picnics and photography with snow-capped mountain and rhododendron surroundings. Freezes in winter; spiritual importance in local Buddhist tradition.
facts: Ideal for short drives and walks

name: Gorsam Chorten
description: Large ancient Buddhist stupa near Zemithang, one of the biggest in Arunachal Pradesh. Modeled after Boudhanath in Nepal; built possibly 12th-18th century by local Monpa monks. Venue for annual Gorsam Kora festival.
facts: Near Zemithang, about 90-100 km from Tawang
Features prayer wheels and circumambulation path

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main base for exploring Tawang's monasteries, lakes and passes. High-altitude town with Monpa culture, markets, and gateway services; connected via NH-13 through Sela Pass or Tunnel.
